items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: everybody in the band, they just fell out... Johnny Ardito, all the guys.

ctx.x: That’s like Louis Armstrong when he first joined Fletcher Henderson, the famous story—he was playing in the big band, reading the part and he sees the symbol, “pp” and he hits it real hard and he’s shouting over the whole band and they said, “What are you doing, Louis?” And he says, well he thought it said, “pound plenty.”
(laughs) Pound plenty. Oh, there are so many incidents that happen in life that are unforgettable but everybody in the band, they just fell out, they just absolutely fell out. He was

getting ready to give a downbeat and I says, “Wait a minute, Nelson, I see a term here that’s sort of insulting to me, ‘colored’. What do you mean by that, are you trying to tell me something?” And everybody fell out, Johnny Ardito, all the guys. He said, “No, that’s a musical term, you know, ‘color,’ ‘color it.’” So I said, “Well, I didn’t see that in ‘One O’Clock Jump.’”
